competitive_landscape: The Playa del Carmen ↔ Cozumel channel is run by high-frequency diesel catamaran ferries (Ultramar, Winjet) carrying very large daily passenger volumes, plus cruise tenders. Fast but fume-heavy and rough in north winds; no premium or electric tier exists.

journeys.today: ~35–45 min on a busy diesel catamaran, rough and fume-heavy in north winds.
journeys.with_navier: A fast, silent zero-emission foiling crossing — stable in chop and clean over the reef park.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The ~9.5nm Playa del Carmen ↔ Cozumel channel is a flagship Pioneer II commuter/tourism crossing — short, dense and ideal for an all-electric premium tier alongside the high-volume diesel ferries.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Not required; the channel is well inside Pioneer II range.

precedents.why_it_matters: Proves the commercial N30 in premium tourism transfer service — directly applicable to a high-volume reef channel.

regulatory_note: Operations sit beside the Cozumel Reefs National Marine Park; zero-wake, zero-emission foiling is well suited to protected reef water. Engagement via Mexico's SEMAR/port authority (API Quintana Roo).
seasonality: Year-round cruise and dive demand; peak Dec–Apr. Summer brings heat and a hurricane-season window (Jun–Nov). Winter 'nortes' chop the channel — exactly the conditions foiling smooths.

sources.label: Ultramar — Playa del Carmen / Cozumel ferry

summary: Cozumel is a Caribbean island off Playa del Carmen and among the busiest cruise-ship ports on Earth, world-famous for the Palancar/Mesoamerican reef diving. The Playa del Carmen ↔ Cozumel ferry is one of Mexico's highest-volume passenger water crossings.
tagline: One of the world's busiest cruise islands, a reef-dive capital off the Riviera Maya.
